original_summary: An unnamed, ill and troubled man wanders through Kyoto, unable to find comfort in the things he once enjoyed. At a fruit shop, he buys a lemon and feels happier as he holds, smells, and admires it. He enters Maruzen, a shop he has been avoiding, but soon feels weighed down again by the books and surroundings. He stacks books into a strange tower, places the lemon on top, and leaves, imagining with playful pleasure that it is a bomb that will soon destroy the shop.
seed_elements: Keep the first-person narrator: an ill, anxious man with little money, wandering around Kyoto.
He is drawn to worn, colorful things and finds a special fruit shop on Teramachi Street.
He buys one lemon and its cool feel, bright color, and fresh smell briefly lift his mood.
He goes into Maruzen, where books and other familiar objects soon bring back his heaviness and unease.
He piles books into a tower and carefully places the lemon on top.
He leaves the lemon behind and imagines it as a bomb; no real explosion occurs, and he walks away feeling amused and lighter.
discarded_elements: Long descriptions of run-down streets, shop displays, and the fruit shop's lighting.
Detailed memories of fireworks, glass toys, beads, and other small pleasures.
The narrator's extended thoughts about childhood, poetry, art, and the lemon's symbolic weight.
Specific illness terms, historical references, and detailed descriptions of the books and objects in Maruzen.
conversion_plan: Write a faithful retelling set in Kyoto, keeping the fruit shop, Maruzen, and the lemon-on-books turning point. Use the original first-person point of view, and refer to people by their role or relationship rather than giving them personal names. Simplify descriptions and minor episodes for an English-learning story of about 300–350 words at A2 level.
title: 檸檬
author: 梶井基次郎
